candidates.odia: ହାତୀ ମୁହଁରୁ କଳେ ଖସି ପଡ଼ିଲେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିକୁ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଶହେ ବରଷ ନ୍ୟାୟ
candidates.english_title: An elephant’s mouthful, an ant’s hundred years
candidates.literal_meaning: If a mouthful falls from an elephant’s mouth, an ant has food for a hundred years.
candidates.explanation: The joke makes the same scrap almost nothing to one creature and an enormous provision to another. The dictionary extends the contrast to an elephant-like person leaving a small amount that can sustain many ant-like lives. The hundred years is the saying’s extravagant measure of scale, not a feeding calculation. The comparison can make an overlooked remainder suddenly look substantial.
candidates.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ପାଇଁ କଳେ ମାତ୍ର ଖାଦ୍ୟ, ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ଶହେ ବରଷର ଖୋରାକ—ଏହି ମାପର ତଫାତରେ କଥାଟିର ମଜା। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ହାତୀ ପରି ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଳ୍ପ କିଛି ଛାଡ଼ିଗଲେ ସେଥିରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପରି ଅନେକ ଜୀବ ପୋଷିହେବାର କଥା ଅଛି। ଶହେ ବରଷ ଏଠାରେ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି। ଜଣକ ପାଇଁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣକ ପାଇଁ କେତେ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇପାରେ, ଚିତ୍ରଟି ସେହି ତଫାତ ଦେଖାଏ।
candidates.english_summary: A tiny remainder to one can be a large provision to another.
candidates.odia_summary: ଜଣକର କଳେ ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣକର ବହୁତ ଖୋରାକ।
candidates.example: A large printing shop offers its unused paper offcuts to a small drawing club. Seeing how many sketchbooks they can make, a member quotes the elephant-and-ant analogy. (Original imagined use.)
candidates.context: The dictionary explicitly interprets unequal scale through elephant-like and ant-like figures. This records a comparison, not a claim that people have unequal worth or a historical account of patronage.
candidates.narrative_credit: Explanation adapted and expanded from ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି — Odia Wiktionary.

candidates.odia: ହାତୀ ମୁତି ଦେଲେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପହଁରାଏ ନ୍ୟାୟ
candidates.english_title: An elephant urinates; ants must swim
candidates.literal_meaning: When an elephant urinates, the ants swim.
candidates.explanation: The blunt bodily image makes scale impossible to miss: an ordinary discharge for the elephant becomes a flood for the ants. The dictionary’s gloss goes further than the heading’s swimming and says the smaller creatures drown. The contrast can picture how a large actor’s small action overwhelms those with much less room to absorb it; that application is editorial, rather than a separate use supplied by the dictionary.
candidates.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ମୁତିଦେବା ପରି ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ପହଁରିବାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି କରିଦିଏ। ବଡ଼ ଓ ସାନର ମାପକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଲା ଦେହଜ ଚିତ୍ର ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ବୁଡ଼ିଯିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ବଡ଼ ପକ୍ଷର ଅଳ୍ପ କାମର ପ୍ରଭାବ ସାନ ପକ୍ଷ ପାଇଁ କେତେ ଭାରି ହୋଇପାରେ—ଏପରି ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଚିତ୍ରଟିର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ସାମାଜିକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
candidates.english_summary: An ordinary act at one scale can overwhelm life at another.
candidates.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଜୀବର ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ସାନ ଜୀବ ପାଇଁ ବିପଦ।
candidates.example: A large buyer delays payment by a few days, calling it a minor adjustment. A small supplier struggling to pay workers replies with the elephant-and-ant analogy. (Original imagined use, not a collected application.)
candidates.context: Preserve the coarse bodily image and the difference between heading and gloss. This is a recorded analogy, not modern zoological evidence. The business example is newly composed.
candidates.narrative_credit: Explanation adapted and expanded from ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି — Odia Wiktionary.

candidates.english_title: Ants eating through the jaggery store
candidates.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants eating up the jaggery store.
candidates.explanation: The sweet store is something the ants will keep returning to. The dictionary applies the image to work that must always be guarded carefully against an enemy. Its emphasis is continuing exposure, rather than a single finished loss. Unlike putting an ant in charge of the store, this analogy does not appoint the eater as guardian.
candidates.meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ଘରକୁ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆସିବା ଥରେ ଜଗିଦେଲେ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯିବା ପରି ନୁହେଁ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ ସର୍ବଦା ସାବଧାନତା ସହ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାକୁ ଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ଜୋର ଲଗାତାର ସତର୍କତା ଉପରେ। ଗୁଡ଼ଘରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିକୁ ଜଗୁଆଳି କରିବାର ଅନ୍ୟ ନ୍ୟାୟଠାରୁ ଏହା ଅଲଗା; ଏଠାରେ ଖାଦକକୁ ରକ୍ଷାର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଦେବା କଥା ନାହିଁ।
candidates.english_summary: The source applies the sweet-store image to work needing continuing protection.
candidates.odia_summary: ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ସାବଧାନରେ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର।
candidates.example: A club restores its noticeboard after repeated deliberate damage. When someone says one repair has settled the matter, another member uses the jaggery-store analogy to explain why they still need to watch it. (Original imagined use.)
candidates.context: The source says enemy, not merely accident or ordinary wear. The new example therefore retains deliberate interference. Note1 in this same source is the different guardian/conflict-of-interest analogy; keep the two separate.
candidates.narrative_credit: Explanation adapted and expanded from ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି — Odia Wiktionary.

candidates.english_title: A stream of people like a line of ants
candidates.literal_meaning: The analogy of an ant-line forming.
candidates.explanation: This is a visual comparison rather than a rebuke. The dictionary describes a place where many people gather and compares their movement to a line of ants. The eye follows the continuing file of people. The source does not turn the image into a lesson about obedience, hard work or unquestioning conformity.
candidates.meaning_odia: ଅନେକ ଲୋକ ଏକାଠି ହୋଇ ଧାର ବାନ୍ଧି ଚାଲୁଥିବା ଦୃଶ୍ୟକୁ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ଧାର ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହି ଦୃଶ୍ୟଗତ ସାମ୍ୟକୁ ଧରେ। ଆଖି ଆଗରେ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଚାଲିବାର ଧାରଟି ଲମ୍ବିଯାଏ। ଏଠାରେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ କିମ୍ବା ଶୃଙ୍ଖଳାର ଉପଦେଶ ଯୋଡ଼ିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ।
candidates.english_summary: A moving crowd is pictured as a line of ants.
candidates.odia_summary: ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଚଳନ୍ତି ଧାର ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ଧାର ପରି ଦିଶେ।
candidates.example: Looking down from a terrace as people file towards a fair, someone remarks, “ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ଧାର ଲାଗିବା ନ୍ୟାୟ।” (Original imagined use.)
candidates.context: The headword is preserved in the saved digital witness. The gloss contains the different spelling ପୁମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି; that discrepancy remains in the exact capture rather than being silently repaired. Genre is descriptive analogy.
candidates.narrative_credit: Explanation adapted and expanded from ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି — Odia Wiktionary.

candidates.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants being mad for jaggery.
candidates.explanation: The ants’ pull towards sweetness supplies a picture of someone’s marked eagerness or greed. The dictionary allows both interest and greed, so the comparison need not carry the same accusation on every occasion. A playful comment about enthusiasm can turn sharp when the attraction is self-serving. The object of desire need not be food.
candidates.meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣକୁ ଧରି ଜଣକର ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ କିମ୍ବା ଲୋଭ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଦୁଇଟି ଅର୍ଥର ସୁଯୋଗ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ ପ୍ରତିଥର ଏହାକୁ କଠୋର ଲୋଭର ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିଦେଲେ କଥାର ସ୍ୱର ବଦଳିଯିବ। ଅବସର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ନେଇ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ, କିମ୍ବା ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳତାକୁ ବିନ୍ଧିପାରେ।
candidates.english_summary: An attraction can be playful eagerness or pointedly described greed.
candidates.odia_summary: ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ ବା ଲୋଭକୁ ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସହ ତୁଳନା।
candidates.example: A friend who never misses a book sale is already at the door before it opens. A companion laughs and uses the ants-and-jaggery analogy. (Original imagined use, choosing the source’s interest rather than greed sense.)
candidates.context: The dictionary explicitly supplies interest or greed as applications. The new example chooses interest; no origin story, popularity measurement or universal claim about ant behaviour is added.
candidates.narrative_credit: Explanation adapted and expanded from ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି — Odia Wiktionary.
